entries.reason: a departure from 12.0 in the start: iOS 12 starts the wrapped session through a method of its own that this release does not have, so the session is started as the SFAuthenticationSession of iOS 11 is, over the page of this package
entries.effect: the session is made with a URL, a callback scheme and a completion handler, and is started with -start, which answers YES once and NO while it runs; the handler is given the callback URL with no error when the page reaches the scheme, or nil and an error of ASWebAuthenticationSessionErrorDomain with the code 1 for a cancel, for an address that is not a web address and for a page dismissed by the user; -cancel ends a running session the same way and does nothing to one that has not started
entries.source: AuthenticationServices of the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0: -[ASWebAuthenticationSession initWithURL:callbackURLScheme:completionHandler:] at 0x1aa076000 makes an SFAuthenticationSession whose handler hands the callback URL on and turns any error into code 1 of the domain, -start and -cancel at 0x1aa076200 and 0x1aa076218 forward to it; an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 with a loopback server for what comes out

entries.reason: the page is drawn by the UIWebView of this release, which shares the application's cookie and cache store and has no private mode. The isolation is buildable - the release has one cookie jar per process and no store per web view, so emptying it around a modal sign-in would really isolate one - but doing it without a journal makes every cookie the application owns depend on the process surviving the login, and on a device with a 282 MB jetsam ceiling being killed mid-flow is ordinary; losing every session the user was signed into is worse than not offering the feature. The work is planned, not refused: write the jar to disk before emptying it and restore from that journal at the next launch. Even then it would isolate cookies and the URL cache and not local or database storage, and would have to say so
